You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of review:** Preliminary; based solely on the Seller's cover note, the "Key Negotiated Positions" summary and the Disclosure Letter (as at 22 September 2026). I have not seen the full marked-up SPA, and the data room position is now over six weeks old — several factual items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation) should be refreshed before any position is finalised.

**Headline:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. Almost every liability and risk-allocation term sits at or beyond the Seller-favourable end of our playbook, and several provisions (Clauses 8.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5, 12.3 "all Claims", and the collapse of Fundamental/Title into the general regime) would, in combination, hollow out the warranty package almost entirely. The Disclosure Letter, by contrast, is candid about what is *not* in the data room — and those admissions actually strengthen our hand on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and bonuses.

Note the Seller's framing ("agreed price mechanics", "negotiated positions", "considered settled", "considered adequate"). None of these characterisations has been confirmed through our authority process and none should be accepted as agreed.

---

## Part A – Liability regime (Clauses 12–13, 9.3, 20.5)

### A1. General Warranty cap – Clause 12.1
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m |

**Issue:** The Seller's number happens to equal our conditional fallback. That is not a reason to accept it. Playbook sec 0.4/6.3 is explicit: a proposed change is not cleared merely because a number matches a fallback. The fallback is available **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft, and no such authority has been given.

**Position:** Reject. Reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team wants to consider conceding the cap later as part of a package (e.g. in exchange for Seller movement on thresholds, Fundamental/Title and the knowledge clause), that is a decision to escalate to Amelia Frost — not something to trade in the mark-up now.

### A2. Thresholds – Clause 12.2
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only ("deductible") | First dollar ("tipping") |

**Issue:** These are 5x our positions on both thresholds, and the Seller has converted the basket from a tipping basket to a deductible. Together they mean the first AUD 250,000 of loss is unrecoverable on any view, and individual claims under AUD 25,000 never count toward the basket. On a AUD 24m business with ~30% revenue concentration in one customer, that is a material erosion.

**Position:** Reject all three elements. Reinstate AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar recovery. Note separately (see A4) that these thresholds must not apply to Fundamental/Title claims at all.

### A3. Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months |

**Issue:** 18 months is, again, exactly our fallback — and again, no Amelia Frost approval has been given. Reinstate 24 months.

**More serious issue – the "all Claims" sweep:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a drafting default that reverses the burden: unless we have affirmatively carved something out, every cap, threshold, time bar and exclusion would apply to Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants. This directly contravenes the playbook's requirement to keep those categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.

**Position:** Delete the "all Claims" default. Replace with the opposite default: the general Warranty limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations, Seller covenants, or claims arising from fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct, except where expressly stated.

### A4. Fundamental / Title Warranties
**Seller:** capacity and title to be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".

**Issue:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title to the shares fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing and would be limited to AUD 4.8m (less AUD 250k basket), claimable only within 18 months, and arguably excluded under Clause 8.3 if the defect was "discoverable from public records". That is an unacceptable outcome and is well outside any market norm for an Australian private M&A deal.

**Position:** Reject. Require a separate Fundamental/Title regime per playbook: 100% of price cap, minimum six-year claims period, outside the de minimis, basket and any buyer-knowledge qualification.

### A5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** apply "to all Claims of any nature".

**Issue:** This is the single most important drafting point in the package. "All Claims of any nature" would extend caps, baskets, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. The playbook requires these to be carved out of *every* limitation to the maximum extent enforceable, and states that no one on our side may waive this. (Separately, attempts to limit liability for fraud are of doubtful enforceability in NSW in any event, but we should not rely on that — the carve-out must be express.)

It would also sweep specific indemnities (e.g. Ironquay, any DD-006 indemnity we negotiate) and the Seller's payment and completion covenants into the general regime.

**Position:** Non-negotiable. Insert an express, overriding carve-out: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for, or operates as an exclusive remedy or non-reliance in respect of, fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers. Narrow Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 so they apply to general Warranty Claims only.

### A6. Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Issue:** The Seller's statement that tax and IP positions are "settled" is an assertion, not an agreement. Our playbook records Tax and IP terms as **OPEN**. Folding them into the general regime (20% cap, 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds) would be a significant adverse resolution of open points by default.

**Position:** Record expressly in our response that Tax and IP terms remain open and are not settled; they are to be dealt with as separate categories with their own cap/time limit (to be negotiated — note the playbook does not authorise unlimited liability on either). Do not let the "all Claims" default in A3 resolve this by silence.

---

## Part B – Disclosure and knowledge

### B1. Disclosure – Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

**Issue:** This is whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure, which the playbook rejects. Combined with a 20% cap and Clause 8.3, it means any matter buried anywhere in the data room — regardless of how it was indexed or whether it was identifiable as a warranty breach — defeats a claim. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is unbounded (ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP registers, land titles?).

**Position:** Reject general disclosure. Require that only matters **fairly disclosed** — in sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the relevant warranty — in the Disclosure Letter itself (with specific cross-references to numbered data room documents) are disclosed. Delete the public-register limb. If a compromise is sought, we could accept disclosure of specifically listed documents (not a blanket index) against specifically identified warranties, but that is a secondary fallback and not in the playbook.

Also note para 1.4 (no admissions). That is standard for a disclosure letter, but it must not be allowed to operate as a *substantive* qualification of warranties — we should confirm the SPA does not give the Disclosure Letter priority over the warranties on matters of legal characterisation (e.g. whether a consent "is legally required").

### B2. Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** no claim for any matter of which the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including any matter "discoverable from the data room or public records".

**Issue:** This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, extended to advisers' knowledge, and further extended to *constructive* knowledge ("discoverable from"). It is broader than the general disclosure clause and would in practice replace the warranties with a caveat emptor regime. Our DD itself becomes the Seller's defence. It also, on its face, applies to title, capacity, fraud and any specific indemnity.

**Position:** Delete Clause 8.3 in its entirety. If the Seller insists on some knowledge concept, the only acceptable form per playbook is a qualifier on *seller* warranties (i.e. "so far as the Seller is aware") limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry — not a bar on buyer claims. No knowledge qualifier of any kind may apply to Title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## Part C – Conditions, completion mechanics and funds flow

### C1. Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
**Seller SPA position:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 2:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue; change-control consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl 11.3; **no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of conditions is in the data room.**

**Issue:** The Disclosure Letter effectively concedes the problem. A written consent that is itself conditional (under cl 11.3) is not an effective consent until those conditions are satisfied. "Satisfied on delivery" would allow Completion against a conditional consent whose conditions may never be met — leaving us owning a business that may lose 30% of revenue. "Reasonable endeavours" is also too weak for a condition precedent of this significance.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent: delivery of an **unconditional** written consent from Bluefen (or a conditional consent **plus** documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen), in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, before Completion.
- Delete "satisfied on delivery".
- Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours to procure the consent, with specific obligations to keep the Buyer informed and not to agree any variation to the Bluefen contract as a price for consent without Buyer approval.
- Ask the Seller for a current status update (the 22 September position is six weeks old).
- Consider whether a Bluefen-specific warranty/indemnity or price adjustment is warranted if consent is delayed, but do not trade away the CP.

### C2. Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
**Seller SPA position:** release "to be provided following Completion".
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 3:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control cl 8.1 and discharge cl 9.2; not repaid, no discharge in data room.

**Issue:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we acquire a company with AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt that is in change-of-control default from the moment we complete (cl 8.1), with security still on foot and no binding commitment from the bank. That exposes the Company to acceleration and enforcement risk and puts the price mechanics at risk if the payout exceeds the deduction assumed.

**Position:**
- Require a **current payout letter** from Riverlark (dated within a few days of Completion) stating the exact amount to repay.
- Repayment **at Completion directly from Completion funds** to Riverlark, as a deduction from the price payable to the Seller, with a **deed of release and discharge of all security** (and PPSR releases) delivered at Completion, held in escrow against receipt of funds if needed.
- A post-completion release is not acceptable under the playbook unless (i) Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds and (ii) Amelia Frost approves in writing. Neither exists. Do not accept the Seller's structure.

### C3. Funds flow / employee bonuses – DD-005
**Seller SPA position:** funds flow reflects "the agreed price mechanics"; AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 5:** bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the draft funds flow**; disclosure is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.

**Issue:** The two statements are in tension. The bonuses are triggered by *our* Completion and will be a liability of the Company (which we will own) when they fall due, unless the Seller funds them. "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless it is contractually hard-wired. Omitting them from the funds flow does not make them go away — it moves the cost to us. Payroll tax, superannuation (if applicable to the bonus character) and other on-costs could add a material percentage on top of AUD 420,000.

Also: the Seller's description of the funds flow as reflecting "agreed" mechanics is not accepted. The funds flow has not been agreed through our authority process.

**Position:**
- Treat the AUD 420,000 **plus** all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee if applicable, any leave loading/other) as either (a) a specific line item deducted from the price in the funds flow and paid through the Company's payroll at/after Completion, or (b) a Seller-funded amount with a Seller covenant and indemnity.
- Require the Seller to confirm the gross-up figure and the on-cost analysis.
- Confirm the bonus arrangements do not include any further Seller-related payments (e.g. transaction bonuses to management) not disclosed in DD-005.
- Reject "agreed price mechanics" language.

### C4. Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
**Seller SPA position:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 4:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Issue:** The risk is not just the AUD 180,000. If any SOW3 fee is unpaid at Completion, IP in the SOW3 Project Materials has not transferred to the Company at all. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover: loss arising from the Company not owning IP it uses or licenses; costs of obtaining a confirmatory assignment; any infringement claim by Ironquay; and any shortfall if the true unpaid amount differs from AUD 180,000 (which neither side has verified). The playbook notes the AUD 180,000 is unverified either way — it could be lower (already paid, in which case we need the receipt) or higher.

**Position:**
- Broaden Clause 11.1 to a specific indemnity for all Loss arising from (i) any failure of IP in SOW3 (and other Ironquay) Project Materials to vest in the Company, (ii) any amount payable to Ironquay in respect of SOW3, and (iii) any claim by Ironquay in relation to the Project Materials.
- Preserve the cure mechanism: Seller to pay all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion and deliver (a) evidence of cleared payment and (b) a confirmatory assignment/acknowledgment from Ironquay that cl 7.3 is satisfied and title has passed.
- Request bank evidence of payment status to replace reliance on DD-010.
- Ensure this indemnity is outside the general cap/basket/time limit (see A3/A5).

### C5. Export / privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
**Seller SPA position:** "preliminary operational matter"; not expected to be material.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 6:** download link sent to an unintended external address; possibly ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary.

**Issue:** The Seller's characterisation ("not expected to be material") is an opinion, and the Disclosure Letter itself says the facts are not yet established. Consistent with the playbook we should **not** assume a confirmed eligible data breach, harm, notification duty or any particular number — but equally we should not accept the Seller's downgrade of it. ~1,240 individuals' personal information (business contact data plus activity data) is potentially within the Privacy Act regime and, depending on the customer contracts, could trigger contractual notification obligations (including possibly to Bluefen).

**Position:**
- Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation (link access logs, recall/expiry of the link, confirmation from the recipient); provide written updates to the Buyer; no notification decision or external communication without consulting the Buyer.
- Warranty: Schedule 6 disclosure to be specific to the facts as at Completion (updated from 22 September).
- Specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party claims), sitting outside the general regime. We are not putting a number on it and neither should the Seller — the indemnity should be loss-based.
- Do not accept "preliminary operational matter" as a drafting characterisation in the SPA.

### C6. Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
**Seller SPA position:** ordinary-course operating costs.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 8:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Issue:** The Seller's SPA note asserts "ordinary course" while its own Disclosure Letter declines to say so. Per playbook, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction is warranted, but we need to understand the timing and nature before accepting the characterisation.

**Position:** Request: renewal dates, whether any renewal is already committed/accrued as at the locked-box/completion accounts date, termination rights and notice periods, and whether the three are linked (DD-011 suggests they should be read together). Depending on the answers: (a) if accrued pre-Completion but unpaid, treat as a working-capital/debt-like item in the completion accounts or price mechanics; (b) if genuinely future ordinary-course, no adjustment but ensure the warranties on material contracts and no unusual commitments are accurate. Keep this open; do not concede "ordinary course" now.

### C7. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Not raised in the Seller's SPA summary, but noted in the Disclosure Letter. Both are described as *not* requiring consent to a share sale (notification only for the lease; assignment restriction only for Mossvale). These should be verified against the actual documents by our team; if correct, require the lease notification to be given pre-Completion (with evidence) and a warranty that no other consent/notification is required. Low priority but should be closed out.

### C8. Title – DD-012
**Seller SPA position:** title evidenced by the Company share register.
**Seller Disclosure Letter para 10:** register records Harbourglass as 100% holder; Seller expressly notes this does not state that the Buyer has verified title.

**Issue:** The share register is an internal Company document controlled by the Seller. It is the starting point, not proof. Combined with Clause 8.3 ("discoverable from public records") and the attempt to cap Title warranties at 20%/18 months, the Seller is offering minimal title protection on a AUD 24m purchase.

**Position:**
- Independent verification before Completion: current ASIC company extract (and historical extract to trace share transfers), PPSR search against the Company and against the Seller for security over the shares, confirmation that Riverlark's security does not extend to the shares (or is released at Completion), executed share transfer form and share certificate(s), board minutes approving the transfer and register update, and Seller corporate authority evidence (constitution, board/shareholder approval, director identities via ASIC).
- Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, no options/rights over shares — on the separate regime (A4), unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.
- Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.

---

## Part D – Cross-cutting observations

1. **Cumulative effect.** Individually, several of the Seller's terms might be arguable; together (20% cap + AUD 250k deductible + 18 months + whole-data-room disclosure + constructive buyer-knowledge exclusion + all limitations applying to all claims including title and fraud) they would leave a warranty package with very little practical value. Our response should make this point expressly rather than negotiating each clause in isolation.

2. **"Agreed" / "settled" / "negotiated" language.** Reject the characterisation in the cover note and the summary heading. Record in our response that no term is agreed until signed, and in particular that the cap, time limits, Tax, IP and funds flow are open.

3. **Fallback discipline.** Two of the Seller's numbers (20% cap, 18 months) coincide with our conditional fallbacks. Neither has been authorised. The mark-up should reinstate the playbook starting positions on both. Any decision to concede is for Amelia Frost in writing, identifying the draft.

4. **Stale facts.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Before signing, require a bring-down: updated disclosure letter, updated DD-006 investigation status, Bluefen and Riverlark status, Ironquay payment evidence, and refreshed ASIC/PPSR searches.

5. **Disclosure Letter is helpful.** Paragraphs 2–6 and 10 are unusually frank admissions of gaps. We should cite them back to the Seller in support of the CP, funds flow and title positions, and ensure they are preserved (not overwritten by a "cleaner" later version).

---

## Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

| # | Item | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Insert express overriding carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. **Non-negotiable; no one on our side may waive.** |
| 2 | Fundamental / Title warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside de minimis/basket/knowledge. Reject "administrative simplicity". |
| 3 | "All Claims" default (cl 12.3) | Delete. Reverse the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnities/payments/covenants separate. |
| 4 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Delete entirely. No adviser or constructive knowledge; no bar on title/capacity/fraud/indemnities. |
| 5 | Disclosure (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2) | Reject data-room and public-register general disclosure; require specific fair disclosure only. |
| 6 | General cap (cl 12.1) | Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% not authorised (no Amelia Frost approval). |
| 7 | Thresholds (cl 12.2) | Reinstate AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 tipping basket, first-dollar recovery. |
| 8 | Claims period (cl 12.3) | Reinstate 24 months. 18 not authorised. |
| 9 | Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | CP = effective consent **and** evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, pre-Completion. Delete "satisfied on delivery". Strengthen endeavours obligation. Request status update. |
| 10 | Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Current payout letter; repay at Completion from Completion funds; security releases at Completion. Post-completion release not acceptable without irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval (neither exists). |
| 11 | Employee bonuses / funds flow | AUD 420,000 + on-costs as a specific line item or Seller-funded with covenant/indemnity. Reject "agreed price mechanics". |
| 12 | Ironquay (cl 11.1) | Broaden to loss-based indemnity covering IP vesting, payments and claims; preserve SOW3 cure (pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion); obtain bank evidence of payment status. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | Log preservation, investigation, Buyer updates, loss-based specific indemnity outside general regime. Assume no breach/harm/notification duty; reject "not material" characterisation. |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Record as OPEN; reject "settled under the general regime". Separate categories to be negotiated; no unlimited liability. |
| 15 | Title (DD-012) | Independent verification (ASIC, PPSR, transfers, authority evidence) before Completion; register is not proof. |
| 16 | Sandbar renewals | Request timing/termination/accrual detail; keep open; no automatic Debt classification or deduction. |
| 17 | Process | Require bring-down disclosure and refreshed facts before signing; reject "agreed/final/settled" characterisations; escalate any fallback decisions to Amelia Frost in writing. |

**Next step:** I recommend we prepare a buyer mark-up of the Seller's summary reflecting items 1–8 as reinstated playbook positions and items 9–15 as drafting proposals, together with a short information request to the Seller covering the stale-fact items (Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment evidence, DD-006 investigation status, Sandbar renewal terms, on-cost analysis for bonuses, and title searches). I can draft either on request.
=== END ADVICE ===
